findings.title: Care supports a non-retaliatory boundary
findings.claim: The focus peace word can carry a non-retaliatory and protective departure from threat, while the promised intercession remains grounded in experienced divine care rather than retaliation.
findings.mechanism: The focus salām carrier meets the supplied commands to say peace while turning away and to endure hostile words with a gracious separation at 43:89 and 73:10. The focus istighfār carrier meets forgiveness, protection from punishment, and Abraham's bounded prayer contacts at 4:110, 13:6, 9:114, 26:86, and 60:4, while 6:54 joins directed peace to divine mercy. Together these contacts let care warrant a boundary without turning the petition into retaliation or self-authorized forgiveness.
findings.reader_payoff: The reply holds goodwill and distance together: peace limits the encounter, the request for forgiveness remains active, and the final care clause explains why the speaker can leave without answering threat in kind.
findings.containment: The ordinary translation remains intact. This does not claim that the father reconciles, that forgiveness is guaranteed, or that every salām is a political settlement; the wider targets provide exact Arabic but not target morphology, so the global relation is qualified.

epistemic.reason: The supplied focus publication is trusted and explicitly anchors the three branches. The wider connection targets provide exact Arabic and authored relation notes but omit target morphology, so the integrated global relation remains qualified rather than lexical certainty.

branch_activations.activation: The wider peace-under-separation contacts meet the focus's addressed salām, so the utterance can set a non-retaliatory limit while the speaker leaves the threat.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Peace is a boundary-setting departure that leaves goodwill in place rather than answering threat with retaliation.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not claim that the father reconciles, that every salām is a political settlement, or that separation itself is the lexical meaning of salām.

findings.title: Salām as a protective state
findings.claim: The focus salām can also be heard as a protected condition that keeps harm at a distance during a hostile separation, alongside its social-peace reading.
findings.mechanism: The focus nominal salām is directed toward a threatened person. The supplied 8:61 target places peace within a conflict setting and joins it to reliance on God, while 6:54 joins a directed salām to divine mercy and forgiveness. Those contacts return through the focus salām and change its effect from social settlement alone toward protection from harm.
findings.reader_payoff: The peace word acquires a practical edge: it can make room for withdrawal without making the addressee exposed to the speaker's retaliation.
findings.containment: This uses the accepted safety facet of salām, not the social-reconciliation branch, the divine-name facet, or the esenlik-yurdu facet. Target morphology is not supplied, so the wider relation remains qualified.

epistemic.reason: The exact target Arabic and connection notes supply conflict, reliance, peace, and mercy contacts, but the connection records have no source-trust label or target morphology.

findings.title: Salām as a directed greeting

findings.reader_payoff: The opening becomes something spoken over a person: a good wish that can be uttered even when the relationship does not become agreement.
findings.containment: This uses only the person-directed greeting facet of the qualified salām record. It does not identify every salām as the same greeting, infer the divine-name or esenlik-yurdu facets, or supply target morphology.

epistemic.reason: The target Arabic and authored notes provide several directed-greeting contacts, while target morphology and a separate connection trust label are absent.

findings.mechanism: The focus qāla carrier brings the reply into voiced, completed speech. The supplied 33:70 target joins speech to upright conduct, 43:89 joins saying peace to turning away, and 17:53 asks for the best speech to prevent divisive escalation. These wider speech acts return through the focus reporting verb and change the opening from a neutral narrative frame into a deliberate ethical utterance.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears the response as chosen conduct in speech: the words themselves perform restraint before the promise of intercession is made.
findings.containment: This retains the ordinary reporting function of qāla and does not make the verb itself mean peace, forgiveness, or departure. Target morphology is not supplied, so only the supplied speech-act contacts are used.

epistemic.reason: The focus surface and exact target Arabic provide a concrete speech-act contact, but the wider connection targets omit target morphology and source-trust labels.

The supplied 31:15 and 29:8 targets pair parental kindness with refusal of an idolatrous demand, while 64:14 places family hostility beside pardoning and forgiving. These wider family-care contacts return through the focus's care predicate and make attention compatible with a firm relational boundary.
findings.reader_payoff: Care is no longer confused with surrender: the relationship can retain goodwill while refusing the demand that would cross its governing limit.
findings.containment: This is a wider family-care pattern, not an identification of all target persons with the focus addressee. It does not replace the direct divine-care reading or claim that kindness removes the need for separation; target morphology is not supplied.

epistemic.reason: The target Arabic and authored notes provide explicit parent-kindness, refusal, hostility, and forgiveness contacts, but the cross-ayah records omit target morphology and source-trust labels.

findings.title: Kāna makes care a sustained relation
findings.claim: The kāna bī ḥafiyyan clause can also present divine care as an established relational condition that warrants the future petition rather than as a one-time compliment.
findings.mechanism: The focus perfect copula carries the state of being graciously attentive toward Ibrahim. The supplied 9:114 target repeats kāna around Abraham's forgiveness promise and its limit, 26:86 places Abraham's prayer for his father beside a kāna statement, and 71:10 places seeking forgiveness beside kāna and a forgiving attribute. These repeated being-and-forgiveness contacts return through the focus copula and make the final care clause a remembered basis for action.
findings.reader_payoff: The closing assertion becomes more than praise after the fact: it explains why the speaker can continue to seek forgiveness even while the encounter is being bounded.
findings.containment: This stays within the copular being and state-reporting branch. It does not activate creation, location, suretyship, or submission meanings of ك و ن, and the target morphology remains unavailable.

epistemic.reason: The focus and target Arabic visibly repeat kāna with forgiveness and relational predicates, but target morphology and a connection source-trust label are not supplied.

findings.title: Attention remains open to petition
findings.claim: An exploratory residue of the focus ḥafiyyan carrier can make divine attention feel available to a continuing request, so the future promise to seek forgiveness remains open to repeated petition rather than closing as a courtesy.
findings.mechanism: The focus ḥafiyyan analysis supplies directed gracious attentiveness with inquiry-residue, while the focus istighfār form is itself a request. The supplied 71:10 target urges seeking forgiveness, 51:18 depicts it as a regular practice, and 71:28 extends parent-directed forgiveness prayer. These wider request patterns return through the focus care predicate and provide an independent petition field for its qualified persistence edge.
findings.reader_payoff: The final care clause can be felt as availability: the petition is not merely announced once but remains able to return to a responsive source.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory functional echo, not a secure lexical rendering of ḥafiyyan as insistence, questioning, or repeated solicitation. The anchorless HFT summary is not used as proof, and target morphology is not supplied.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus carrier and independent target Arabic request patterns provide a concrete contact, but the persistence step is interpretive and the target morphology and connection trust labels are absent.
